title: Disable inactive users
use_case: On a schedule, disable cloud-only users in Entra ID with no successful sign-in for 30 days, or the days you set, without Sophos ITDR. It needs only the Microsoft Graph API connection. Users synced from Active Directory are listed for you to disable there.
trigger: Generic Trigger, Playbook Usage Playbook Schedule. Then add a schedule with More Actions > Schedule Executions, such as daily with the cron expression 0 2 * * *
connections: Taegis.MicrosoftGraphAPI 2.12.2, the Microsoft Graph API connector Sophos manages, to find inactive users, read their directory roles and disable cloud-only accounts
requires: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2, a Microsoft Graph app with User.Read.All, AuditLog.Read.All, Directory.Read.All and User.EnableDisableAccount.All, and Sophos Fusion playbooks under Security Operations > Automations
mdr_note: Sophos MDR doesn't run or watch this playbook, and it doesn't change what Sophos MDR does.
rollback: Enable User: enable the account again in Entra ID, and add it to Excluded users so a later run doesn't disable it again.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: This playbook disables cloud-only users in Entra ID with no successful sign-in for the days you set, 30 by default, and lists synced users for you to disable in Active Directory. A schedule starts it, and it calls only the Microsoft Graph API connector Sophos manages, with dry run on, only the domains you list in scope and at most 10 users a run. It needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2, and not Sophos ITDR.
notes:
Setup:
- It doesn't need Sophos ITDR. Sign-in activity needs Entra ID P1 or P2 and AuditLog.Read.All.
- It needs only the Microsoft Graph API connection. Version 1.0.0 also disabled synced users through the LDAP connection, and needed both connections. Version 2.0.0 is a major version, so a playbook configured from 1.0.0 doesn't move to it on its own.
- Set Look-back days to at least the days between runs. Each run then sees only users who became inactive lately, so disabled accounts drop out.
- Graph returns one page per search, 100 users by default. For accounts already inactive when you start, set Look-back days to 0 for a few runs.
- It doesn't disable anything in Active Directory. With Sophos ITDR, Disable dormant users in Active Directory disables dormant on-premises and synced accounts there, on ITDR's own thresholds.
- There's no approval step. Dry run, Domains, Excluded users and Max users per run are the controls.

How it works:
- It searches Microsoft Graph for users whose last successful sign-in, interactive or not, is before midnight UTC Days without a sign-in ago. Graph allows no other filter with sign-in activity, so the playbook drops disabled users, guests and other domains.
- Include users with no sign-in on record adds users with none since December 2023, or ever, created before the cut-off.
- It disables cloud-only users in Entra ID. It lists a synced user as skipped, because Entra Connect Sync would undo a disable in Entra ID, so you disable it in Active Directory.
- It never disables a user with an Entra ID directory role or in a role-assignable group. An eligible PIM role that isn't active doesn't count.
- The result is the execution's outcome under Playbooks > Executions.

Testing:
- Not run in a tenant yet.
- On 2026-11-03 this version's dsl passed playbookValidateDSLV2 with no errors or warnings in a Sophos Fusion test tenant. It wasn't imported. On 2026-11-02 a renamed copy of version 1.0.0 imported and exported again unchanged.
- Every step ran in Sophos Fusion's CEL engine, through its evaluateExpr API, in 11 made-up runs: cloud-only, synced, role holders, excluded, guests, other domains, no sign-in on record, the per-run limit, refused disables and a failed search.

Known gaps:
- A real Graph search is untested: whether Graph takes the sign-in activity filter with the $count=true and ConsistencyLevel eventual searchUser always sends, the Look-back days date range, and eq null. A refusal ends the run in FAIL with Graph's message.
- Whether a schedule passes the playbook's settings is untested. Check them in the schedule's Playbook Inputs.
- How the engine runs the per-user loop is untested. It follows the Sophos-managed templates.
- Saving it with only the Microsoft Graph API connection is untested. Sophos Fusion asks for a connection to each connector a template lists, and this one lists only that one.
